services.name: Amazon EC2
services.definition: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) lets you rent virtual computers, called instances, in the cloud. You pick the CPU, memory and operating system, and pay only while it runs.
usedFor: Running software that needs a full server you control
Scaling capacity up or down as traffic changes

scenario.story: The bakery's online ordering site ran on one old office PC. They moved it to a small EC2 instance, then switched to a bigger instance type for the December rush and back again in January.

services.name: AWS Lambda
services.definition: Lambda runs your code without you managing any servers. You upload a function, choose what triggers it, and pay only for the milliseconds it runs.
usedFor: Reacting to events like file uploads or database changes
Building lightweight APIs and back ends
Automating scheduled tasks and glue code

scenario.story: Every time a user uploads a photo to SnapFrame, a Lambda function automatically creates a thumbnail. During quiet hours it costs almost nothing; on viral days it handles thousands of uploads a minute.

services.name: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
services.definition: Elastic Beanstalk takes your application code and deploys it for you, setting up servers, load balancing and scaling automatically. You focus on code, not infrastructure.
usedFor: Deploying web apps quickly without learning every AWS service
Running Java, Python, Node.js, .NET, PHP, Ruby or Go apps
Getting built-in health monitoring and rolling updates

scenario.story: A two-person team built a tutoring marketplace in Python. They uploaded it to Elastic Beanstalk, which created the servers and load balancer, so they launched in an afternoon instead of a week.

services.name: Amazon Lightsail
services.definition: Lightsail is the simplest way to get a virtual server, database or website on AWS, with a fixed, predictable monthly price.
usedFor: Hosting simple websites, blogs and WordPress
Small business apps and dev/test servers
Learning cloud basics with a friendly console

scenario.story: The dental office needed a website with a booking form. Their part-time IT helper launched a WordPress instance on Lightsail for a low flat monthly fee, with no surprise bills.

services.name: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
services.definition: EC2 Auto Scaling automatically adds or removes EC2 instances based on demand or a schedule, so you have enough capacity without paying for idle servers.
usedFor: Replacing unhealthy instances without human action
Saving money by scaling in during quiet periods

scenario.story: When concert tickets go on sale, TicketDash's traffic jumps tenfold in minutes. An Auto Scaling group grows from 4 to 40 instances, then shrinks back once the rush ends.

services.name: AWS Batch
services.definition: AWS Batch runs large numbers of computing jobs for you, queuing them up and picking the right amount of compute to finish them efficiently.
usedFor: Rendering video or images in bulk

scenario.story: HelixGen needs to analyze thousands of DNA samples each week. They submit each sample as a Batch job, and Batch spins up hundreds of instances, finishes the work, then shuts them down.

services.name: EC2 Image Builder
services.definition: Image Builder automates creating, patching and testing server images (AMIs) and container images, so every new server starts from an up-to-date, secure template.
usedFor: Building 'golden images' with your company's standard software
Applying security patches to images on a schedule
Testing images before they are used in production

scenario.story: Auditors require every server to start fully patched. NorthBank uses Image Builder to produce a new hardened image every week, and Auto Scaling launches servers only from the latest image.

services.name: AWS Outposts
services.definition: Outposts brings AWS hardware into your own data center, so you can run AWS services on-premises with the same tools and APIs you use in the cloud.
usedFor: Apps that need very low latency to on-site systems
Keeping data in a specific location for regulations

scenario.story: A car factory's robots need responses in single-digit milliseconds. Precision Motors installed an Outposts rack on the factory floor to run its control software locally while managing it like the rest of AWS.

services.name: AWS Wavelength
services.definition: Wavelength places AWS compute inside telecom providers' 5G networks, so mobile apps can reach servers with extremely low delay.
usedFor: Live video analytics for connected devices

scenario.story: ArenaVerse's AR sports game overlays live stats on a stadium view. Running its game servers in Wavelength zones cut lag enough that the overlays keep up with the action on the field.

services.name: AWS ParallelCluster
services.definition: ParallelCluster is an open-source tool that builds high-performance computing (HPC) clusters on AWS, like a supercomputer you can create and delete on demand.
usedFor: Engineering simulations like crash tests and fluid dynamics
Large research workloads that need many connected servers

scenario.story: Engineers at BlueCurrent simulate how wind turbines behave in storms. They spin up a 500-core cluster with ParallelCluster for a few days, then tear it down instead of buying their own supercomputer.

services.name: Amazon ECS
services.definition: Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS) runs and manages Docker containers for you. You describe which containers to run, and ECS keeps them running and healthy.
usedFor: Batch and background jobs in containers
Modernizing apps without managing a container platform

scenario.story: ShopNest split its online store into separate cart, search and payment services. Each runs as a container on ECS, so the team can update search without touching payments.

services.name: Amazon EKS
services.definition: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) runs Kubernetes, the popular open-source container platform, for you, so you don't have to install or maintain its control plane.
usedFor: Running Kubernetes apps without managing control-plane servers
Moving existing Kubernetes workloads to AWS
Running the same platform across cloud and on-premises

scenario.story: StreamWave already used Kubernetes in its own data center. Moving to EKS let them keep their existing tools and manifests while AWS handled the upgrades and availability of the cluster.

services.name: AWS Fargate
services.definition: Fargate is a serverless engine for containers: it runs your ECS or EKS containers without you choosing, patching or scaling any servers.
usedFor: Running containers without managing EC2 instances
Isolating each task for stronger security

scenario.story: QuickQuote's quote engine runs in containers. With Fargate they just set CPU and memory per task, and they no longer spend Fridays patching container host servers.

services.name: Amazon ECR
services.definition: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) is a private, secure place to store and share your container images, similar to a private Docker Hub.
usedFor: Storing container images used by ECS, EKS and Lambda
Sharing images across accounts and Regions

scenario.story: Every time ShopNest's build pipeline finishes, it pushes the new container image to ECR. ECR scans it for vulnerabilities before ECS is allowed to deploy it.

services.name: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
services.definition: ROSA is a fully managed Red Hat OpenShift container platform running on AWS, jointly supported by Red Hat and AWS.
usedFor: Moving OpenShift apps from on-premises to the cloud
Enterprise Kubernetes with Red Hat tooling

scenario.story: Continental Rail's ticketing apps ran on OpenShift in an aging data center. Moving to ROSA let developers keep the same workflows while the platform team stopped managing hardware.

services.name: Amazon S3
services.definition: Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) stores any amount of files, called objects, in containers called buckets. It is extremely durable and you pay only for what you store.
usedFor: Storing images, videos, backups and documents
Building data lakes for analytics and machine learning

scenario.story: SnapFrame stores billions of user photos in S3. Popular photos stay in S3 Standard, while photos untouched for a year move automatically to a cheaper storage class.

services.name: Amazon S3 Glacier
services.definition: S3 Glacier storage classes are very low-cost S3 storage for data you rarely need, such as archives, with retrieval times from milliseconds to hours.
usedFor: Long-term archives kept for legal or compliance reasons
Storing old media and research data cheaply

scenario.story: The hospital must keep patient imaging for years. Scans older than 90 days move to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, cutting storage costs dramatically while still being retrievable if needed.

services.name: Amazon EBS
services.definition: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) provides virtual hard drives, called volumes, that attach to EC2 instances and keep their data even when the instance stops.
usedFor: Boot drives and data disks for EC2
Databases running on EC2 that need fast disks

scenario.story: LedgerLite runs its accounting database on EC2 with a high-performance EBS volume. Nightly EBS snapshots let them restore the database to any recent day in minutes.

services.name: Amazon EFS
services.definition: Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) is a shared network drive in the cloud that many servers and containers can read and write at the same time. It grows and shrinks automatically.
usedFor: Shared files for web servers behind a load balancer
Content management systems and home directories

scenario.story: Pagewise runs its CMS on six servers. All of them mount the same EFS file system, so an image uploaded through any server appears instantly on all of them.

services.name: Amazon FSx
services.definition: FSx provides fully managed file systems built on popular technologies, including Windows File Server, Lustre, NetApp ONTAP and OpenZFS.
usedFor: Windows file shares for business apps (FSx for Windows)
Very fast storage for HPC and ML (FSx for Lustre)
Moving NetApp or ZFS storage to the cloud

scenario.story: The architecture firm's designers share huge CAD files over Windows file shares. FSx for Windows File Server gave them the same mapped drives they were used to, without an office file server.

services.name: AWS Storage Gateway
services.definition: Storage Gateway connects your on-premises systems to AWS storage, letting local apps save files, volumes or virtual tapes that end up in the cloud.
usedFor: Extending office file servers into S3
Replacing physical tape backup with virtual tapes
Hybrid storage during a gradual cloud move

scenario.story: Hartwell's office file server kept running out of space. A File Gateway now keeps recent files cached locally while storing everything in S3, so the server never fills up again.

services.name: AWS Backup
services.definition: AWS Backup is a central place to schedule, manage and monitor backups across many AWS services, such as EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS and S3.
usedFor: One backup policy for all your resources
Copying backups to another Region or account for safety

scenario.story: Instead of separate scripts for every database and disk, LedgerLite created one AWS Backup plan: daily backups, kept 35 days, with a copy sent to a second Region.

services.name: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
services.definition: Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously copies your servers to AWS so you can quickly recover them there if your data center or primary Region fails.
usedFor: Low-cost disaster recovery for on-premises servers
Recovering from ransomware with point-in-time copies

scenario.story: A flood warning hit Midland's warehouse data center. Because their servers were replicated with Elastic Disaster Recovery, they launched them in AWS within an hour and kept shipping orders.

services.name: Amazon RDS
services.definition: Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) runs traditional SQL databases like MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle and SQL Server for you, handling backups, patching and failover.
usedFor: Databases for web and business applications
Moving an existing SQL database to the cloud
High availability with Multi-AZ standby copies

scenario.story: The bakery's order database lived on the same server as its website. Moving it to RDS for MySQL gave them automatic nightly backups and a standby copy in another data center.

services.name: Amazon Aurora
services.definition: Aurora is AWS's cloud-built relational database, compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, designed for higher performance and availability than a standard database.
usedFor: High-traffic apps that outgrow a single database
Global apps with read copies in several Regions
Serverless databases that scale with demand (Aurora Serverless)

scenario.story: TicketDash's MySQL database struggled on sale days. After moving to Aurora MySQL with several read replicas, seat searches stayed fast even with a million fans online.

services.name: Amazon Aurora DSQL
services.definition: Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database that can run active in multiple Regions at once, scaling automatically with virtually no infrastructure to manage.
usedFor: Apps that must keep writing even if a Region goes down
PostgreSQL-compatible apps that need effortless scaling

scenario.story: PayStream processes payments for customers on three continents. With Aurora DSQL running in multiple Regions, payments keep flowing even during a regional outage.

services.name: Amazon DynamoDB
services.definition: DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database that stores data as key-value items and returns results in milliseconds at any scale, with no servers to manage.
usedFor: Shopping carts, user profiles and session data

scenario.story: PlayForge's mobile game stores each player's inventory in DynamoDB. When the game hit the top of the app store, DynamoDB scaled from hundreds to millions of requests without any changes.

services.name: Amazon ElastiCache
services.definition: ElastiCache is a managed in-memory cache (Valkey, Redis OSS or Memcached) that keeps frequently used data in memory so apps respond much faster.

scenario.story: NewsPulse's homepage ran the same database queries thousands of times a second. Caching the results in ElastiCache cut page load times in half and reduced database load.

services.name: Amazon MemoryDB
services.definition: MemoryDB is a durable, Redis- and Valkey-compatible in-memory database. It is as fast as a cache but safely stores data across multiple data centers.
usedFor: Apps that need cache speed without risking data loss

scenario.story: FlashCart runs lightning sales where stock must be accurate to the second. Its inventory counts live in MemoryDB, giving microsecond reads with no risk of losing data on a failure.

services.name: Amazon DocumentDB
services.definition: DocumentDB is a managed document database compatible with MongoDB, storing flexible JSON-like documents instead of rows and columns.
usedFor: Moving MongoDB workloads to a managed service

scenario.story: RecipeBox stores recipes with different ingredients, steps and photos. Their MongoDB code worked with DocumentDB with few changes, and they stopped managing database servers.

services.name: Amazon Keyspaces
services.definition: Keyspaces is a serverless, managed database compatible with Apache Cassandra, built for large-scale apps that need fast reads and writes.
usedFor: Moving Cassandra workloads without managing clusters

scenario.story: FleetTrack logs GPS points from 50,000 delivery vans. They moved their self-managed Cassandra cluster to Keyspaces and no longer get paged at night for node failures.

services.name: Amazon Neptune
services.definition: Neptune is a managed graph database that stores relationships between things, such as people, products or accounts, and lets you query those connections quickly.
usedFor: Fraud detection by finding suspicious connections
Knowledge graphs for search and generative AI

scenario.story: KinConnect's 'people you may know' feature needed to explore friends-of-friends instantly. Storing the social graph in Neptune turned a slow multi-join SQL query into a fast graph lookup.

services.name: Amazon Timestream
services.definition: Timestream is a managed time-series database for data that arrives over time, like sensor readings or app metrics, with built-in time-based queries.
usedFor: IoT sensor data and industrial telemetry

scenario.story: GreenLeaf's greenhouses send temperature and humidity readings every 10 seconds. Timestream stores the readings and powers a dashboard showing trends over the past hour, day and season.

services.name: Amazon VPC
services.definition: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is your own private, isolated network inside AWS, where you control IP addresses, subnets, routing and firewalls.
usedFor: Separating public web servers from private databases
Controlling traffic with security groups and network ACLs
Connecting cloud resources securely to your office

scenario.story: LedgerLite put its web servers in public subnets and its database in private subnets of a VPC. The database can't be reached from the internet at all, only from the web tier.

services.name: Amazon Route 53
services.definition: Route 53 is AWS's DNS service: it turns names like example.com into the addresses of your servers, and can route users to healthy or nearby endpoints.
usedFor: Registering domain names and managing DNS
Failing over to a backup site automatically
Routing users to the closest or fastest Region

scenario.story: TutorLink registered its domain with Route 53. Health checks watch the main site, and if it ever goes down, Route 53 automatically sends visitors to a static 'we'll be right back' page in S3.

services.name: Amazon CloudFront
services.definition: CloudFront is a content delivery network (CDN) that caches your website, videos and APIs in hundreds of locations worldwide so users get them faster.
usedFor: Speeding up websites and downloads globally
Protecting origins together with AWS WAF and Shield

scenario.story: StreamWave's viewers in Asia complained about buffering. Serving video through CloudFront meant clips were delivered from nearby edge locations, and buffering complaints dropped sharply.

services.name: Elastic Load Balancing
services.definition: Elastic Load Balancing spreads incoming traffic across multiple servers or containers and stops sending traffic to any that are unhealthy. Types include Application, Network and Gateway Load Balancers.
usedFor: Keeping websites up when one server fails
Routing requests by URL path to different services
Handling millions of connections with low latency

scenario.story: ShopNest's Application Load Balancer sends /cart requests to the cart service and /search requests to the search service, and quietly skips any container that fails a health check.

services.name: Amazon API Gateway
services.definition: API Gateway lets you create, publish and secure APIs, the 'front door' apps use to talk to your back end, without running any servers.
usedFor: REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs for web and mobile apps
Adding authentication, throttling and caching to APIs
Exposing Lambda functions as web endpoints

scenario.story: FitTrack's mobile app calls an API Gateway endpoint to save workouts. API Gateway checks the user's login token, limits abusive clients and passes valid requests to Lambda.

services.name: AWS Direct Connect
services.definition: Direct Connect is a private, dedicated network connection from your data center or office to AWS that doesn't travel over the public internet.
usedFor: Meeting rules that forbid internet-based connections

scenario.story: NorthBank moves terabytes of trading data to AWS every night. A Direct Connect link gives them steady, predictable throughput that their internet connection couldn't guarantee.

services.name: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
services.definition: Site-to-Site VPN creates an encrypted tunnel over the internet between your office or data center network and your AWS VPC.
usedFor: Backup path for a Direct Connect link

scenario.story: Hartwell needed its office to reach a document system in AWS securely. A Site-to-Site VPN was set up in a day using the office's existing firewall.

services.name: AWS Client VPN
services.definition: Client VPN lets individual employees securely connect from their laptops to AWS and on-premises networks using a VPN app.
usedFor: Reaching private resources in a VPC

scenario.story: When the firm went hybrid-remote, designers used Client VPN to reach the private file servers in AWS from home, with logins tied to the company directory.

services.name: AWS Transit Gateway
services.definition: Transit Gateway is a central network hub that connects many VPCs and on-premises networks, so you don't need a tangled web of individual connections.
usedFor: Connecting dozens or hundreds of VPCs
Sharing one VPN or Direct Connect link across VPCs

scenario.story: Continental Rail had 40 VPCs connected by a confusing mesh of peering links. They replaced the mesh with a single Transit Gateway that every VPC and the data center connect to.

services.name: AWS Global Accelerator
services.definition: Global Accelerator gives your app fixed global IP addresses and routes users over AWS's private global network to the nearest healthy endpoint.
usedFor: Improving performance for global users of TCP/UDP apps
Static IPs that customers can allowlist

scenario.story: ArenaVerse's game servers run in four Regions. Global Accelerator gives players a single pair of IPs and sends them to the closest healthy Region, cutting lag for players worldwide.

services.name: AWS PrivateLink
services.definition: PrivateLink lets you reach AWS services, or services from other companies, privately from your VPC without sending traffic over the public internet.
usedFor: Private access to AWS services via VPC endpoints
Offering your SaaS product privately to customers
Keeping sensitive traffic off the internet

scenario.story: PayStream's customers didn't want payment data crossing the internet. PayStream published its API with PrivateLink, so each customer connects privately from their own VPC.

services.name: AWS Cloud Map
services.definition: Cloud Map is a service registry: your apps register their location, and other apps can look them up by a friendly name instead of hard-coding addresses.
usedFor: Keeping track of constantly changing container IPs

scenario.story: ShopNest's containers come and go many times a day. Each registers itself in Cloud Map, and the cart service always finds the payment service by name.

services.name: Amazon VPC Lattice
services.definition: VPC Lattice connects, secures and monitors communication between services across many VPCs and accounts, without managing complex network plumbing.
usedFor: Simplifying connectivity when IP ranges overlap

scenario.story: MegaMart's 30 teams each own their own AWS accounts. VPC Lattice lets the checkout service call inventory and pricing services across accounts with simple access policies.

services.name: AWS Cloud WAN
services.definition: Cloud WAN lets you build and manage a global network that links your offices, data centers and AWS Regions from one central dashboard and policy.
usedFor: Global corporate networks across many countries
Segmenting traffic like production vs. development worldwide

scenario.story: Atlas Shipping has offices in 25 ports worldwide. Cloud WAN connects every office and AWS Region using one policy, keeping finance traffic separate from guest Wi-Fi traffic.

services.name: AWS IAM
services.definition: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls who can sign in to your AWS account and exactly what they are allowed to do, using users, roles and permission policies.
usedFor: Giving each person or app only the permissions it needs
Letting AWS services act on your behalf with roles

scenario.story: TutorLink's intern needed to view logs but not delete servers. An IAM policy gave read-only access to CloudWatch, and the app servers use an IAM role instead of stored passwords.

services.name: AWS IAM Identity Center
services.definition: IAM Identity Center gives employees one login to access all your AWS accounts and business apps, often connected to an existing directory like Microsoft Entra ID or Okta.
usedFor: Single sign-on across many AWS accounts
Assigning permission sets by job role

scenario.story: MegaMart's engineers used to juggle logins for 60 AWS accounts. With IAM Identity Center they sign in once with their company account and pick the account and role they need.

services.name: Amazon Cognito
services.definition: Cognito adds sign-up, sign-in and user management to your web and mobile apps, including social logins like Google or Apple.
usedFor: Giving app users temporary AWS credentials

scenario.story: FitTrack needed user accounts with 'Sign in with Apple' and password resets. Cognito handled all of it, so the team didn't have to build or secure its own login system.

services.name: AWS KMS
services.definition: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) creates and controls the encryption keys used to protect your data, and records every time a key is used.
usedFor: Encrypting S3, EBS, RDS and other data at rest
Controlling who can decrypt sensitive data
Meeting compliance requirements for key management

scenario.story: Every patient record Riverside stores is encrypted with a KMS key. Only the clinical app's role may use the key, and CloudTrail logs each decryption for auditors.

services.name: AWS Secrets Manager
services.definition: Secrets Manager securely stores passwords, API keys and other secrets, and can rotate them automatically so they never sit unchanged in your code.
usedFor: Storing database passwords outside of code

scenario.story: A developer accidentally committed a database password to Git. After that, LedgerLite moved all credentials to Secrets Manager, which now rotates the password every 30 days.

services.name: AWS Certificate Manager
services.definition: Certificate Manager provides free public SSL/TLS certificates for your AWS-hosted websites and renews them automatically, enabling the padlock (HTTPS) in browsers.
usedFor: HTTPS for load balancers, CloudFront and API Gateway
Managing private certificates for internal apps

scenario.story: Their site once went down because a certificate expired. Now ACM issues the certificate for their load balancer and renews it automatically, so it never expires again.

services.name: AWS CloudHSM
services.definition: CloudHSM gives you dedicated, single-tenant hardware security modules in AWS, where you alone control the encryption keys.
usedFor: Strict compliance needing dedicated key hardware

scenario.story: Card network rules required PayStream to keep keys in dedicated hardware it controls. CloudHSM met the requirement without PayStream buying and racking its own HSM appliances.

services.name: AWS WAF
services.definition: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that blocks malicious web requests, such as SQL injection, bots and attacks from specific countries or IPs.
usedFor: Protecting websites and APIs from common exploits
Blocking traffic by location or IP

scenario.story: Bots were buying up limited sneakers within seconds. FlashCart added AWS WAF bot-control and rate-limiting rules to its CloudFront distribution, giving real shoppers a fair chance.

services.name: AWS Shield
services.definition: Shield protects your applications against DDoS attacks, which try to overwhelm a site with traffic. Shield Standard is automatic and free; Shield Advanced adds more protection and expert help.
usedFor: Automatic protection from common network attacks
Advanced DDoS protection with 24/7 response team

scenario.story: During a major election night, NewsPulse was hit by a large DDoS attack. Shield Advanced absorbed the flood and the AWS response team helped tune defenses while the site stayed online.

services.name: Amazon GuardDuty
services.definition: GuardDuty is a threat-detection service that continuously watches your AWS logs and activity for signs of hackers, malware or compromised credentials.
usedFor: Detecting unusual API calls or logins
Finding malware in EC2 volumes and S3

scenario.story: GuardDuty alerted PlayForge that a server was talking to a known crypto-mining address. The leaked key was revoked and the instance replaced within the hour.

services.name: Amazon Inspector
services.definition: Inspector automatically scans EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.

scenario.story: When a critical bug was announced in a popular library, Inspector showed QuickQuote within minutes exactly which of its 300 containers and functions were affected.

services.name: Amazon Macie
services.definition: Macie uses machine learning to find sensitive data, such as names, credit card numbers or passport numbers, stored in your S3 buckets and alerts you to risks.
usedFor: Supporting GDPR, HIPAA and PCI compliance
Finding publicly accessible buckets with sensitive data

scenario.story: A Macie scan found a forgotten S3 bucket containing student contact lists. TutorLink locked it down and set up regular scans to catch similar mistakes early.

services.name: AWS Security Hub
services.definition: Security Hub collects security findings from many AWS services and partner tools into one dashboard and checks your accounts against best-practice standards.
usedFor: A single view of security alerts across accounts
Triggering automatic fixes for common issues

scenario.story: MegaMart's security team used to check five different consoles. Security Hub now gathers GuardDuty, Inspector and Macie findings from every account into one prioritized list.

services.name: Amazon Detective
services.definition: Detective helps you investigate security incidents by automatically linking logs and activity into visual timelines, so you can find the root cause faster.
usedFor: Understanding what a compromised user or role did

scenario.story: After the crypto-mining alert, PlayForge used Detective to trace which IAM key was used, from which IP, and every other resource it touched in the previous week.

services.name: AWS Firewall Manager
services.definition: Firewall Manager centrally sets up and enforces firewall rules, like WAF rules, security groups and Network Firewall policies, across all accounts in your organization.
usedFor: Consistent WAF protection on every account

scenario.story: New teams kept launching websites without WAF. Firewall Manager now automatically attaches MegaMart's standard WAF rules to every new load balancer in every account.

services.name: AWS Network Firewall
services.definition: Network Firewall is a managed firewall for your VPCs that inspects and filters network traffic, including blocking traffic to bad domains.
usedFor: Filtering outbound internet traffic by domain

scenario.story: Regulators asked NorthBank to restrict which websites servers can reach. Network Firewall now allows outbound traffic only to an approved list of software-update domains.

services.name: AWS Artifact
services.definition: Artifact is a self-service portal where you download AWS's compliance reports, such as SOC and ISO certifications, and accept agreements like a HIPAA BAA.

scenario.story: Before going live, Riverside's compliance officer downloaded AWS's SOC 2 report from Artifact and accepted the HIPAA Business Associate Addendum in a few clicks.

services.name: AWS Audit Manager
services.definition: Audit Manager continuously collects evidence about how your AWS resources are configured and maps it to audit frameworks, making audits far less painful.
usedFor: Preparing for SOC 2, PCI DSS or GDPR audits

scenario.story: PayStream's PCI audit used to take weeks of screenshots. Audit Manager now gathers the evidence automatically, and auditors review a ready-made report.

services.name: AWS Directory Service
services.definition: Directory Service runs Microsoft Active Directory in AWS for you, or connects AWS to your existing on-premises Active Directory.
usedFor: Joining Windows servers in AWS to a domain
Using company AD logins with AWS services

scenario.story: The firm's Windows apps relied on Active Directory. AWS Managed Microsoft AD let their cloud servers and WorkSpaces use the same staff logins as the office.

services.name: AWS Resource Access Manager
services.definition: Resource Access Manager lets you securely share AWS resources, such as subnets or Transit Gateways, with other AWS accounts instead of duplicating them.
usedFor: Sharing a central network with many accounts

scenario.story: Continental Rail's network team owns the Transit Gateway. Using RAM, they share it with every application account so teams can connect without building their own.

services.name: AWS Verified Access
services.definition: Verified Access gives employees secure access to internal apps without a VPN, checking each request's user identity and device security first (a 'zero trust' approach).
usedFor: Per-app access rules based on user and device

scenario.story: QuickQuote replaced its VPN for claims adjusters. Now Verified Access checks that each adjuster is logged in and their laptop is managed before opening the claims app.

services.name: Amazon Security Lake
services.definition: Security Lake automatically gathers security logs from AWS, on-premises and third-party sources into a data lake in your account, in a standard format.
usedFor: Feeding security tools with consistent data

scenario.story: Atlas Shipping's analysts needed a year of logs to investigate threats. Security Lake collects CloudTrail, VPC and firewall logs into one queryable lake in a common format.

services.name: Amazon Verified Permissions
services.definition: Verified Permissions manages fine-grained permissions inside your own applications, using readable policies written in the Cedar language.
usedFor: Deciding what each app user can see or do
Moving authorization rules out of application code
Consistent access rules across many apps

scenario.story: Hartwell's case app must ensure lawyers see only their own clients' files. Verified Permissions evaluates a Cedar policy on every request instead of scattered if-statements in code.

services.name: AWS Private Certificate Authority
services.definition: AWS Private CA lets you create your own private certificate authority to issue certificates for internal servers, devices and services.
usedFor: Certificates for internal apps and microservices

scenario.story: Every greenhouse sensor needs its own certificate to prove its identity. GreenLeaf issues them from a Private CA, and revokes any sensor that is stolen.

services.name: Amazon CloudWatch
services.definition: CloudWatch collects metrics and logs from your AWS resources and apps, shows them on dashboards and sends alarms when something looks wrong.
usedFor: Monitoring CPU, memory, errors and latency
Alarms that notify people or trigger auto-scaling

scenario.story: A CloudWatch alarm fires if checkout errors rise above 1%. The on-call engineer gets paged and uses CloudWatch Logs to find the bad deployment in minutes.

services.name: AWS CloudTrail
services.definition: CloudTrail records every action taken in your AWS account, such as who did what, when and from where, creating an audit trail.

scenario.story: A production database was mysteriously deleted. CloudTrail showed exactly which user made the call and when, which led to tighter IAM permissions.

services.name: AWS Config
services.definition: AWS Config keeps a history of how your resources are configured and checks them against rules, flagging anything non-compliant such as an unencrypted disk.
usedFor: Enforcing rules like 'all S3 buckets must be private'

scenario.story: A Config rule checks that every EBS volume is encrypted. When someone launches an unencrypted one, Config flags it and the security team is notified automatically.

services.name: AWS Systems Manager
services.definition: Systems Manager is a toolbox for operating your servers at scale: patching, running commands, storing settings and logging in securely without opening SSH ports.
usedFor: Secure shell access with Session Manager

scenario.story: Midland patches 800 servers every month using Systems Manager Patch Manager, and engineers use Session Manager to log in, so no SSH ports are open to the internet.

services.name: AWS CloudFormation
services.definition: CloudFormation lets you describe your AWS infrastructure in a template file (YAML or JSON) and creates it automatically, an approach called infrastructure as code.
usedFor: Building identical dev, test and production environments
Deploying across many accounts and Regions with StackSets

scenario.story: QuickQuote's whole environment, including VPC, load balancer, containers and database, lives in CloudFormation templates. Spinning up a new test environment takes 20 minutes and zero clicks.

services.name: AWS Organizations
services.definition: Organizations lets you manage many AWS accounts together, with consolidated billing and guardrail policies (SCPs) that apply to every account.
usedFor: Separating teams and environments into accounts
One combined bill with volume discounts
Blocking risky actions across all accounts

scenario.story: MegaMart groups its accounts by business unit in Organizations. A service control policy prevents anyone from turning off CloudTrail, in any account.

services.name: AWS Control Tower
services.definition: Control Tower sets up a secure, well-organized multi-account AWS environment (a 'landing zone') in a few steps, with built-in guardrails and an account factory.
usedFor: Quickly setting up multi-account best practices
Vending new accounts with standard settings

scenario.story: As FitTrack grew to 10 teams, it used Control Tower to create a landing zone. New team accounts now come pre-configured with logging, security and budget alerts.

services.name: AWS Trusted Advisor
services.definition: Trusted Advisor inspects your AWS account and gives recommendations to save money, improve security, increase performance and avoid hitting service limits.
usedFor: Spotting security gaps like open ports
Warning before you reach service quotas

scenario.story: Trusted Advisor pointed out two forgotten test servers and an unused load balancer. Removing them cut the bakery's monthly AWS bill noticeably.

services.name: AWS Service Catalog
services.definition: Service Catalog lets IT teams publish a menu of approved, pre-configured AWS products that employees can launch themselves with a few clicks.

scenario.story: Data scientists at NorthBank can launch an approved, pre-secured analytics workspace from Service Catalog without waiting days for an IT ticket.

services.name: AWS Health Dashboard
services.definition: The AWS Health Dashboard shows the status of AWS services and alerts you to events, such as outages or scheduled maintenance, that affect your specific resources.
usedFor: Checking if an AWS issue is affecting you

scenario.story: When an EC2 host needed retirement, the Health Dashboard warned TutorLink a week in advance, so they moved the instance during a quiet hour instead of being surprised.

services.name: AWS Compute Optimizer
services.definition: Compute Optimizer analyzes how your resources are actually used and recommends better-sized EC2 instances, EBS volumes, Lambda functions and containers.
usedFor: Finding cheaper or faster instance types

scenario.story: Compute Optimizer showed that LedgerLite's servers averaged 8% CPU. Switching to smaller instances saved money with no performance impact.

services.name: AWS License Manager
services.definition: License Manager helps you track and enforce software licenses, like Microsoft or Oracle, across AWS and on-premises to avoid overuse and penalties.
usedFor: Preventing launches that exceed license limits

scenario.story: Continental Rail owns 200 SQL Server licenses. License Manager blocks new launches beyond that number, avoiding expensive surprises during a vendor audit.

services.name: AWS Well-Architected Tool
services.definition: The Well-Architected Tool walks you through questions about your workload and compares it to AWS best practices across six pillars, highlighting risks to fix.
usedFor: Finding reliability, security and cost risks

scenario.story: Before a big marketing campaign, FitTrack ran a Well-Architected review. It revealed their database had no backups in another Region, which they fixed before launch.

services.name: Amazon Managed Grafana
services.definition: Managed Grafana runs the popular open-source Grafana dashboards for you, letting teams visualize metrics, logs and traces from many data sources.

scenario.story: StreamWave's engineers loved Grafana but hated maintaining it. Managed Grafana gave them the same dashboards, connected to CloudWatch and Prometheus, with no servers to patch.

services.name: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus
services.definition: This service stores and queries metrics using Prometheus, the open-source monitoring standard for containers, without you running Prometheus servers.

scenario.story: StreamWave's EKS clusters send metrics to Managed Prometheus, which scales automatically as they add clusters, and feeds their Grafana dashboards.

services.name: AWS Resilience Hub
services.definition: Resilience Hub assesses whether your application can meet its recovery goals (how fast and with how little data loss) and recommends improvements.
usedFor: Checking recovery time and recovery point targets

scenario.story: PayStream set a goal of recovering within 15 minutes. Resilience Hub found a single-AZ cache that broke that goal, and recommended a multi-AZ setup.

services.name: AWS Management Console
services.definition: The Management Console is the web interface where you sign in and manage all your AWS services through point-and-click screens.

scenario.story: The dental office's IT helper does everything in the Management Console, from checking the website server to reviewing the monthly bill, without writing any code.

services.name: AWS Support Plans
services.definition: AWS Support offers plans from free Basic support to Business, Enterprise On-Ramp and Enterprise, adding faster response times, technical experts and account guidance.
usedFor: Proactive guidance from a technical account manager (Enterprise)

scenario.story: Because outages during big sales are costly, TicketDash pays for Business Support. When a strange networking issue hit, they reached an AWS engineer by phone within an hour.

services.name: AWS Cost Explorer
services.definition: Cost Explorer shows charts of your AWS spending over time, broken down by service, account or tag, and forecasts future costs.
usedFor: Seeing which services cost the most

scenario.story: SnapFrame's bill jumped 40% one month. Cost Explorer showed the spike came from data transfer, which they fixed by adding CloudFront in front of S3.

services.name: AWS Budgets
services.definition: Budgets lets you set spending limits and sends alerts, or even takes automatic actions, when actual or forecast costs go over them.
usedFor: Alerting when spending exceeds a limit
Tracking reserved instance and savings plan usage

scenario.story: Each research grant has a fixed cloud budget. AWS Budgets emails the lab lead at 80% and 100% of the monthly limit so no grant overspends.

services.name: AWS Pricing Calculator
services.definition: The Pricing Calculator is a free web tool to estimate how much an AWS setup will cost before you build it.
usedFor: Estimating the cost of a new project

scenario.story: Before moving to AWS, the bakery owner used the Pricing Calculator to estimate the monthly cost of a small server and database, and confirmed it fit their budget.

services.name: Savings Plans & Reserved Instances
services.definition: Savings Plans and Reserved Instances give large discounts compared with On-Demand prices in exchange for committing to steady usage for one or three years.
usedFor: Discounts across EC2, Fargate and Lambda (Compute Savings Plans)
Reserving capacity in a specific Availability Zone

scenario.story: LedgerLite's core servers run 24/7, so they bought a 1-year Compute Savings Plan. Their steady compute bill dropped significantly with no technical changes.

services.name: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
services.definition: Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to spot unusual spikes in your AWS spending and alerts you quickly, before they become large bills.

scenario.story: A test script accidentally launched 50 large GPU instances. Cost Anomaly Detection flagged the spike the same day, saving PlayForge from a huge end-of-month bill.

services.name: AWS Data Exports (Cost & Usage Report)
services.definition: Data Exports delivers your most detailed billing data, including the Cost and Usage Report, to S3, where you can analyze it with tools like Athena or QuickSight.

scenario.story: MegaMart's finance team exports detailed cost data to S3 and queries it with Athena to charge each department for exactly what it uses.

services.name: AWS Billing Conductor
services.definition: Billing Conductor lets you customize how AWS costs are shown and grouped, for example to create your own rates for internal teams or resale customers.
usedFor: Showback and chargeback with custom rates

scenario.story: CloudCrafters manages AWS for 40 small businesses. Billing Conductor lets them produce a custom bill for each client, including their own service margin.

services.name: AWS Marketplace
services.definition: AWS Marketplace is an online catalog where you can find, buy and deploy third-party software and data that runs on AWS, billed through your AWS account.
usedFor: Buying security, monitoring or database software
Consolidating vendor bills into AWS billing

scenario.story: QuickQuote needed a third-party firewall appliance. They subscribed through AWS Marketplace, launched it in minutes, and it appears on their regular AWS bill.

services.name: Amazon Athena
services.definition: Athena lets you run standard SQL queries directly on files stored in S3, with no servers or databases to set up. You pay per query based on data scanned.
usedFor: Ad-hoc analysis of logs and data lakes
Querying CSV, JSON and Parquet files in S3

scenario.story: NewsPulse stores website clickstream logs in S3. Editors use Athena to ask questions like 'which articles were read most yesterday?' with simple SQL.

services.name: Amazon Redshift
services.definition: Redshift is a fast, managed data warehouse that analyzes huge amounts of structured data using SQL, ideal for business reporting.
usedFor: Analyzing billions of sales or event records
Combining warehouse and data lake queries

scenario.story: MegaMart loads every sale from 900 stores into Redshift each night. Morning reports on sales by region and product are ready before stores open.

services.name: Amazon EMR
services.definition: EMR runs big-data frameworks like Apache Spark, Hive and Presto on managed clusters or serverlessly, to process massive data sets.
usedFor: Machine learning feature engineering at scale

scenario.story: FleetTrack processes a year of GPS data to find the most efficient delivery routes. EMR runs the Spark job across 100 nodes in a few hours, then the cluster shuts down.

services.name: AWS Glue
services.definition: Glue is a serverless data integration service that discovers, catalogs, cleans and transforms data (ETL) so it is ready for analytics and machine learning.
usedFor: ETL jobs that prepare data for analysis
A central Data Catalog of your tables

scenario.story: RecipeBox's raw app events arrive messy. A nightly Glue job cleans them, converts them to Parquet, and registers tables in the Data Catalog for Athena.

services.name: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
services.definition: Kinesis Data Streams collects and stores streaming data, like clicks or sensor readings, in real time so multiple apps can process it within seconds.
usedFor: Feeding live dashboards and fraud detection

scenario.story: Every in-game action is sent to Kinesis Data Streams. One app updates live leaderboards while another looks for cheating patterns, both from the same stream.

services.name: Amazon Data Firehose
services.definition: Data Firehose is the easiest way to load streaming data into destinations like S3, Redshift or OpenSearch, with no code needed for delivery.
usedFor: Delivering logs and events to S3
Converting data formats on the way

scenario.story: NewsPulse sends clickstream events to Data Firehose, which batches them, converts them to Parquet and drops them into S3 every few minutes for Athena.

services.name: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
services.definition: This service runs Apache Flink applications that analyze streaming data in real time, for example calculating rolling averages or detecting patterns as data arrives.

scenario.story: PayStream uses a Flink app to watch card transactions in real time. If one card is used in two countries within minutes, the app flags it instantly.

services.name: Amazon MSK
services.definition: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) runs Apache Kafka, a popular event-streaming platform, without you managing Kafka clusters.
usedFor: Moving existing Kafka workloads to AWS

scenario.story: Atlas Shipping's container-tracking events flow through Kafka. Moving to MSK removed the burden of patching and scaling brokers from their small platform team.

services.name: Amazon OpenSearch Service
services.definition: OpenSearch Service runs OpenSearch, a search and analytics engine for full-text search, log analysis and vector search used in AI apps.
usedFor: Search boxes for websites and apps

scenario.story: RecipeBox's search bar used to be slow and literal. With OpenSearch, searching 'quick chiken pasta' finds the right recipes despite the typo, in milliseconds.

services.name: Amazon QuickSight
services.definition: QuickSight is a business intelligence service for building interactive dashboards and reports, including asking questions about data in plain English.

scenario.story: The bakery owner opens a QuickSight dashboard each morning to see yesterday's best-selling items and plan how much dough to prepare.

services.name: AWS Lake Formation
services.definition: Lake Formation helps you build a secure data lake and manage fine-grained permissions, down to specific columns and rows, from one place.
usedFor: Central permissions for data lake tables
Hiding sensitive columns from some users

scenario.story: Researchers query Riverside's data lake, but Lake Formation hides patient names and addresses from them, while billing staff can see those columns.

services.name: Amazon DataZone
services.definition: DataZone is a data management service where teams can catalog, discover, share and govern data across the organization, like an internal data marketplace.
usedFor: Finding trusted data sets across teams

scenario.story: MegaMart's marketing analysts used to email around asking for data. Now they search the DataZone catalog, find the 'loyalty members' data set and request access in one click.

services.name: AWS Clean Rooms
services.definition: Clean Rooms lets companies analyze their combined data together without either side seeing the other's raw data.
usedFor: Collaborative research without sharing raw records

scenario.story: FlashCart and an advertising partner wanted to know how many ad viewers bought products. Clean Rooms gave them the overlap counts without exchanging customer lists.

services.name: AWS Data Exchange
services.definition: Data Exchange lets you find, subscribe to and use third-party data sets, like weather, financial or location data, directly in AWS.
usedFor: Enriching your data with market data

scenario.story: GreenLeaf subscribes to a weather data set through Data Exchange, so their models can combine forecasts with greenhouse sensor data.

services.name: Amazon Kinesis Video Streams
services.definition: Kinesis Video Streams securely streams video from cameras and devices to AWS for storage, playback, and analysis with machine learning.

scenario.story: SafeNest's smart doorbells stream video to Kinesis Video Streams. Homeowners watch live from their phones, and clips are analyzed to detect package deliveries.

services.name: Amazon SageMaker AI
services.definition: SageMaker AI is a platform to build, train and deploy machine learning models, providing notebooks, training infrastructure and hosted model endpoints in one place.

scenario.story: QuickQuote's data scientists trained a model to estimate claim costs in SageMaker AI, then deployed it as an endpoint that the quote app calls in real time.

services.name: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
services.definition: Ground Truth helps you label data, such as drawing boxes around objects in images, to create the training data that ML models learn from.
usedFor: Combining human labelers with automatic labeling

scenario.story: To teach a model to spot plant disease, GreenLeaf used Ground Truth to have workers label 20,000 leaf photos as healthy or diseased.

services.name: Amazon Bedrock
services.definition: Bedrock gives you access to leading generative AI foundation models from Amazon and other AI companies through one API, so you can build AI features without managing models.
usedFor: Answering questions over your documents (RAG with Knowledge Bases)

scenario.story: Hartwell built an internal assistant on Bedrock that answers lawyers' questions using the firm's own precedent documents, with Guardrails blocking confidential client data from responses.

services.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
services.definition: AgentCore provides the building blocks to run AI agents securely in production, including runtime, memory, identity, tool access and observability, for agents built with any framework.
usedFor: Giving agents secure access to tools and APIs

scenario.story: Atlas Shipping built an agent that answers 'where is my container?' by calling tracking APIs. AgentCore hosts it, remembers each customer's context and logs every tool call.

services.name: Amazon Q Developer
services.definition: Q Developer is a generative AI assistant for software developers and IT teams that helps write, explain, test and upgrade code, and answers questions about AWS.

scenario.story: TutorLink's junior developer used Q Developer in their IDE to generate unit tests and explain an unfamiliar part of the codebase, finishing a feature in half the time.

services.name: Amazon Q Business
services.definition: Q Business is a generative AI assistant for employees that answers questions, summarizes content and completes tasks using your company's own data and apps.
usedFor: Answering HR, policy and IT questions
Searching across wikis, drives and tickets

scenario.story: Midland connected Q Business to its policy wiki and file shares. Warehouse managers now ask 'what's our overtime policy?' and get an answer with a link to the source.

services.name: Amazon Rekognition
services.definition: Rekognition analyzes images and videos with pre-trained AI, detecting objects, text, faces and unsafe content, with no machine learning expertise needed.
usedFor: Detecting objects and labels in media

scenario.story: SnapFrame uses Rekognition to automatically flag inappropriate photos before they appear in public feeds, reducing the moderation team's workload.

services.name: Amazon Comprehend
services.definition: Comprehend uses natural language processing to find meaning in text, such as sentiment, key phrases, topics, languages and personal information.
usedFor: Detecting and redacting personal data in text

scenario.story: FitTrack runs app store reviews through Comprehend each week. The product team instantly sees whether sentiment improved after each release.

services.name: Amazon Textract
services.definition: Textract automatically extracts printed text, handwriting, tables and form fields from scanned documents and PDFs.

scenario.story: Customers upload photos of repair invoices. Textract pulls out the totals and line items, so claims are processed in minutes instead of days.

services.name: Amazon Transcribe
services.definition: Transcribe converts speech in audio and video files or live streams into text, with support for many languages and speaker identification.

scenario.story: StreamWave uses Transcribe to generate subtitles for every new show, making content accessible and searchable.

services.name: Amazon Polly
services.definition: Polly turns text into lifelike speech in dozens of languages and voices.

scenario.story: NewsPulse adds a 'listen to this article' button powered by Polly, so commuters can hear stories while driving.

services.name: Amazon Translate
services.definition: Translate provides fast, natural-sounding machine translation of text between dozens of languages.

scenario.story: ShopNest expanded to Spain and Brazil by running its product descriptions through Translate, then having native speakers review only the top sellers.

services.name: Amazon Lex
services.definition: Lex lets you build conversational chatbots and voice bots that understand what users want and respond, the same technology behind Alexa.
usedFor: Voice bots for phone lines with Amazon Connect

scenario.story: A Lex chatbot on the dental office's website handles appointment rescheduling at any hour, so staff spend less time on the phone.

services.name: Amazon Kendra
services.definition: Kendra is an intelligent enterprise search service that understands natural-language questions and finds answers across your company's documents.

scenario.story: Maintenance crews type 'how do I reset the door sensor on model X trains?' and Kendra finds the exact page across thousands of PDF manuals.

services.name: Amazon Personalize
services.definition: Personalize creates real-time personalized recommendations, like 'you might also like', using the same type of technology Amazon.com uses.

scenario.story: StreamWave feeds viewing history to Personalize, which powers the 'Because you watched...' row and increased time spent watching.

services.name: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I)
services.definition: Augmented AI adds human review to machine learning predictions, sending low-confidence results to people to check.

scenario.story: When Textract is unsure about an invoice amount, A2I sends it to a claims clerk to confirm, keeping accuracy high without reviewing everything by hand.

services.name: AWS HealthLake
services.definition: HealthLake stores, transforms and analyzes health data in the industry-standard FHIR format, helping healthcare organizations make sense of medical records.
usedFor: Storing patient data in FHIR format
Extracting medical information from clinical notes

scenario.story: Riverside loads patient records into HealthLake to identify patients at risk of diabetes and invite them for early screening.

services.name: Amazon SQS
services.definition: Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) is a message queue: one part of your app drops messages in, another part picks them up and processes them when it's ready.

scenario.story: When orders flood in, the website puts each order in an SQS queue. The kitchen-printing system works through the queue steadily, so no order is ever lost.

services.name: Amazon SNS
services.definition: Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) sends a message to many subscribers at once (publish/subscribe), including other apps, email, SMS or mobile push.
usedFor: Fan-out of events to multiple services

scenario.story: When an order is placed, TicketDash publishes one SNS message. The email service, the fraud checker and the analytics pipeline each receive their own copy.

services.name: Amazon EventBridge
services.definition: EventBridge is a serverless event bus that routes events from your apps, AWS services and SaaS tools to the right targets based on rules, and can run scheduled jobs.
usedFor: Reacting to AWS events like 'instance stopped'

scenario.story: When a user finishes a 30-day streak, an event goes to EventBridge, which triggers a Lambda to award a badge and a Step Functions flow to send a reward email.

services.name: AWS Step Functions
services.definition: Step Functions coordinates multiple steps of a process into a visual workflow, handling retries, errors and waiting, so you don't write that logic yourself.
usedFor: Orchestrating Lambda functions and AWS services

scenario.story: ShopNest's checkout is a Step Functions workflow: charge the card, reserve stock, create the shipment, and automatically refund if any step fails.

services.name: Amazon MQ
services.definition: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker for Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ, so existing apps using standard messaging protocols can move to AWS without rewriting.
usedFor: Migrating apps that use ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ
Industry-standard protocols like AMQP, MQTT and JMS

scenario.story: Continental Rail's legacy ticketing system talks over ActiveMQ. Amazon MQ let them move it to AWS without changing a single line of messaging code.

services.name: Amazon AppFlow
services.definition: AppFlow moves data securely between SaaS apps like Salesforce, Slack or Zendesk and AWS services like S3 or Redshift, with no code.
usedFor: Syncing CRM data into a data lake

scenario.story: TutorLink's sales team lives in Salesforce. AppFlow copies new leads to S3 every hour so analysts can combine them with app usage data.

services.name: Amazon MWAA
services.definition: Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA) runs Apache Airflow, a popular tool for scheduling and orchestrating data pipelines, without managing servers.
usedFor: Moving existing Airflow workflows to AWS

scenario.story: HelixGen's nightly pipeline has 40 dependent steps. MWAA runs their existing Airflow DAGs, retrying failed steps and alerting the team only when needed.

services.name: AWS CodePipeline
services.definition: CodePipeline automates the steps to release software (build, test and deploy) every time you change your code, known as continuous delivery.
usedFor: Connecting source, build and deploy tools

scenario.story: Every time a developer merges code, CodePipeline builds it, runs tests, deploys to staging, waits for a manager's approval, then releases to production.

services.name: AWS CodeBuild
services.definition: CodeBuild compiles source code, runs tests and produces software packages, using fresh build servers that scale automatically and cost nothing when idle.
usedFor: Running CI jobs without managing build servers

scenario.story: ShopNest retired its overloaded Jenkins server. CodeBuild now runs dozens of builds in parallel, so developers no longer wait in a queue.

services.name: AWS CodeDeploy
services.definition: CodeDeploy automates deploying application updates to EC2, on-premises servers, Lambda and ECS, with strategies like rolling and blue/green to avoid downtime.
usedFor: Gradual traffic shifting for Lambda and ECS

scenario.story: TicketDash deploys with CodeDeploy blue/green. If error alarms fire after the switch, CodeDeploy automatically routes traffic back to the old version.

services.name: AWS CodeArtifact
services.definition: CodeArtifact is a managed repository for software packages (like npm, PyPI and Maven) so teams can store and share approved libraries securely.
usedFor: Controlling which open-source packages are allowed

scenario.story: NorthBank developers install packages only through CodeArtifact, which caches approved open-source versions and hosts the bank's internal libraries.

services.name: AWS X-Ray
services.definition: X-Ray traces requests as they travel through your application's services, showing where time is spent and where errors happen.
usedFor: Finding slow parts of distributed apps

scenario.story: Checkout felt slow but every service looked fine alone. X-Ray traces revealed the payment service was calling a fraud API three times per request.

services.name: AWS CDK
services.definition: The AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK) lets you define cloud infrastructure using familiar programming languages like TypeScript or Python, then deploys it through CloudFormation.
usedFor: Infrastructure as code in a real programming language

scenario.story: FitTrack's developers prefer TypeScript over YAML. With CDK they built a reusable 'API service' component that each team uses to launch new services in a few lines.

services.name: AWS SAM
services.definition: The AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM) is a framework with a short template syntax and CLI for building, testing and deploying serverless apps.
usedFor: Defining Lambda functions, APIs and tables concisely
Deploying serverless apps with one command

scenario.story: SnapFrame's thumbnail service is a SAM template of 30 lines. Developers test the function locally with SAM CLI, then run 'sam deploy' to ship it.

services.name: AWS CLI
services.definition: The AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) lets you control AWS services by typing commands in a terminal, which makes it easy to script and automate tasks.
usedFor: Managing resources quickly from a terminal

scenario.story: Pagewise's admin wrote a short CLI script that copies the day's uploaded images to a backup bucket every night.

services.name: AWS CloudShell
services.definition: CloudShell is a browser-based terminal inside the AWS Console, already signed in with your permissions and preloaded with the AWS CLI and common tools.
usedFor: Running CLI commands without installing anything

scenario.story: The IT helper needed to run one CLI command from a borrowed laptop. CloudShell opened a ready-to-use terminal in the browser in seconds.

services.name: AWS Fault Injection Service
services.definition: Fault Injection Service runs controlled 'chaos engineering' experiments, such as stopping instances or adding latency, to test how your app copes with failures.

scenario.story: PayStream used Fault Injection Service to shut down one Availability Zone in a test. They discovered a hard-coded address and fixed it before a real outage could expose it.

services.name: AWS Amplify
services.definition: Amplify is a set of tools to build, connect and host full-stack web and mobile apps quickly, including hosting, authentication, data and storage.
usedFor: Hosting React, Vue, Next.js and other web apps
Adding login, APIs and storage to apps

scenario.story: RecipeBox's front-end team connected their Git repo to Amplify Hosting. Every pull request gets its own preview URL, and merges go live automatically.

services.name: AWS AppSync
services.definition: AppSync lets you create managed GraphQL and real-time APIs, so apps can fetch exactly the data they need from multiple sources in one request.
usedFor: GraphQL APIs for web and mobile apps
Real-time updates like live chat or scores
Offline data sync for mobile apps

scenario.story: ArenaVerse's app shows live match scores. AppSync subscriptions push updates to every fan's phone the instant a goal is scored.

services.name: AWS Device Farm
services.definition: Device Farm tests your mobile and web apps on real phones, tablets and browsers hosted by AWS, so you don't need a drawer full of devices.
usedFor: Automated testing on many real devices

scenario.story: A crash only happened on certain older Android phones. Device Farm ran FitTrack's tests on 30 real devices and pinpointed the affected models.

services.name: Amazon Location Service
services.definition: Location Service adds maps, address search, routing and geofencing to your apps, while keeping location data private within AWS.
usedFor: Alerts when devices enter or leave an area (geofences)

scenario.story: FleetTrack shows customers a live map of their delivery van and sends an alert when the van enters a geofence around their street.

services.name: AWS Database Migration Service
services.definition: DMS moves databases to AWS quickly and securely while the source database stays running, and can convert between different database engines.
usedFor: Switching engines, e.g. Oracle to PostgreSQL

scenario.story: Continental Rail moved a 4 TB Oracle database to Aurora PostgreSQL. DMS kept the copies in sync for weeks, so the final switch took only minutes of downtime.

services.name: AWS Application Migration Service
services.definition: Application Migration Service 'lifts and shifts' servers from on-premises or other clouds to AWS by continuously copying them and launching them as EC2 instances.

scenario.story: Midland's data center lease was ending. Application Migration Service copied 300 servers to AWS over two months, with each cutover taking under an hour.

services.name: AWS DataSync
services.definition: DataSync moves large amounts of files between on-premises storage, other clouds and AWS storage services quickly, with built-in scheduling and verification.
usedFor: Migrating file shares to S3, EFS or FSx
Copying data for analytics or backup

scenario.story: HelixGen's lab sequencers produce terabytes of data daily. DataSync automatically copies the new files to S3 every night for analysis.

services.name: AWS Transfer Family
services.definition: Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS, FTP and AS2 servers that store files directly in S3 or EFS, for exchanging files with partners.
usedFor: Receiving files from partners over SFTP

scenario.story: Partner banks send daily transaction files over SFTP. Transfer Family receives them straight into S3, where a Lambda function starts processing immediately.

services.name: AWS Snowball
services.definition: Snowball is a rugged physical device AWS ships to you: you load huge amounts of data onto it and ship it back, which can be faster than uploading over the internet.
usedFor: Moving petabytes of data to AWS
Data transfer from sites with poor connectivity

scenario.story: StreamWave had 500 TB of film archives on tapes and disks. Uploading would take months, so they loaded Snowball devices and shipped them to AWS.

services.name: AWS Application Discovery Service
services.definition: Application Discovery Service collects information about your on-premises servers, like their specs, usage and connections, to help plan a migration.
usedFor: Right-sizing AWS resources for migrated servers

scenario.story: Before migrating, Midland used Application Discovery Service and found that two 'unrelated' apps shared a database, so they planned to move them together.

services.name: AWS IoT Core
services.definition: IoT Core securely connects billions of internet-connected devices to the cloud, so they can send data and receive commands.
usedFor: Collecting data from sensors and machines
Routing device data to other AWS services

scenario.story: SafeNest's smart thermostats connect to IoT Core. Homeowners change the temperature from their phone and the command reaches the thermostat in under a second.

services.name: AWS IoT Greengrass
services.definition: Greengrass is software that runs on edge devices, letting them process data and run code or ML models locally, even when offline, while syncing with the cloud.
usedFor: Local processing on factory or field equipment
Running ML models at the edge

scenario.story: Precision Motors runs a defect-detection model with Greengrass on cameras along the assembly line, so faulty parts are flagged instantly even if the internet drops.

services.name: AWS IoT SiteWise
services.definition: IoT SiteWise collects, organizes and analyzes data from industrial equipment, helping factories monitor performance and spot problems.

scenario.story: BlueCurrent streams vibration and speed data from 200 wind turbines into SiteWise, and technicians see which turbines need maintenance before they break.

services.name: AWS IoT Device Defender
services.definition: Device Defender audits the security settings of your IoT devices and watches their behavior to detect anything unusual, such as a hacked device.

scenario.story: Device Defender noticed a batch of doorbells suddenly sending far more data than usual. SafeNest isolated them and pushed a firmware fix.

services.name: AWS IoT Device Management
services.definition: Device Management helps you register, organize, monitor and remotely update large fleets of IoT devices.

scenario.story: GreenLeaf rolled out a firmware update to 5,000 greenhouse sensors in stages using Device Management, starting with 1% to make sure nothing broke.

services.name: Amazon WorkSpaces
services.definition: WorkSpaces provides virtual desktops in the cloud: employees log in from any device to a full Windows or Linux desktop running in AWS.

scenario.story: Hartwell's lawyers access their WorkSpaces desktop from home laptops. Client files never leave AWS, which keeps the firm's insurer happy.

services.name: Amazon AppStream 2.0
services.definition: AppStream 2.0 streams desktop applications to a web browser, so users can run software without installing it on their own computer.
usedFor: Delivering heavy design or engineering software
Software for students on any device

scenario.story: Interns use the firm's CAD software streamed through AppStream 2.0 on basic laptops, instead of the firm buying each of them an expensive workstation.

services.name: Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser
services.definition: WorkSpaces Secure Browser gives employees a secure, cloud-hosted web browser to reach internal websites and SaaS apps, without data being stored on their device.
usedFor: Safe access to internal web apps from any device

scenario.story: Third-party claims assessors use WorkSpaces Secure Browser to access QuickQuote's claims portal, and nothing can be downloaded to their personal laptops.

services.name: Amazon Connect
services.definition: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center: set up phone lines, chat, routing and AI-powered agent help in minutes, paying only for what you use.
usedFor: Customer service phone and chat centers

scenario.story: PayStream set up a support line in Amazon Connect in a day. Calls are routed by language, and agents see live call transcripts and suggested answers.

services.name: Amazon SES
services.definition: Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) sends and receives email at scale, such as order confirmations, password resets and newsletters.

scenario.story: Every ticket purchase triggers an SES email with the tickets attached. SES sends millions of these on big sale days.

services.name: AWS End User Messaging
services.definition: End User Messaging sends SMS, voice and mobile push messages to your customers worldwide, for things like one-time passcodes and alerts.

scenario.story: Patients get an SMS reminder the day before their appointment, sent through End User Messaging, which cut no-shows noticeably.

services.name: Amazon WorkMail
services.definition: WorkMail is a secure, managed business email and calendar service that works with desktop and mobile email apps like Outlook.

scenario.story: The bakery moved from personal email addresses to WorkMail, giving every staff member a professional address and a shared order calendar.
